entries.26956a71a7f1be06: The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] states that the group (the company, 34 consolidated subsidiaries and 3 equity-method affiliates) mainly operates a hotel business and other investment business. In its core hotel business, the company operates and manages hotels in Osaka Prefecture and Tokyo, and is entrusted with the operation of facilities in Kyoto Prefecture and Tokyo. The five hotel facilities listed under “Status of Principal Facilities” are all real estate trust beneficiary interests held by a godo kaisha (limited liability company) and are leased to group companies. The other segment, the other investment business, includes the cemetery business in Malaysia, residential and other real estate development in Australia, domestic real estate leasing and securities investment, under the [[term:segment|segment]] label. Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥9,908 million, of which ¥8,962 million came from the hotel business and ¥946 million from the other investment business. As a future policy, the company states that it will raise the share of management-contract (MC) hotels under an “asset-light strategy” and set a new medium-term target of “30 hotels in five years”.
entries.38749828c32e9555: Entrusted operation of accommodation facilities in Kyoto Prefecture and Tokyo
entries.4799ca938300478c: Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥9,908 million (up 18.3% year on year). Hotel business revenue was ¥8,962 million (up 22.1% year on year), with the opening of “Dorsett by Agora Osaka Sakai” in March 2025 contributing to the revenue increase. On the other hand, “Agora Place Osaka Namba” ended operations at the end of July 2025, but it is stated that the strong performance of existing facilities offset that impact. The other investment business was ¥946 million (down 8.8% year on year), of which the cemetery business in Malaysia was ¥894 million and the securities investment business was ¥27 million.

entries.653317748cda5cb1: The annual securities report states that, as the weaker yen increased foreign visitor arrivals to Japan (42,683,600 for the full year 2025), the company captured strong inbound demand and achieved high-occupancy, high-price operations. In Osaka, the company captured the rise in accommodation demand associated with the Osaka-Kansai Expo. The Malaysian cemetery business is said to have remained firm, against a backdrop of rising demand for suburban cemeteries and columbaria accompanying soaring land prices in urban areas.

For the fiscal year ended December 2025, sales were ¥946 million (down 8.8% from the previous fiscal year) and operating profit was ¥137 million (down 47.9% from the previous fiscal year). Sales are centered on the cemetery business in Malaysia, for which the securities report gives sales of ¥894 million. The securities report explains this segment in its description of business by dividing it into 4 categories, but amounts are stated separately only for the cemetery business and the securities investment business.

entries.834d8861103c0845: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥1,055 million (up 110.3% year on year), and ordinary profit was ¥869 million (up 250.3% year on year). The annual securities report explains that, in addition to higher revenue, cost control through the establishment of an efficient operating structure contributed. Profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥1,274 million, exceeding ordinary profit. The annual securities report states that this is due, among other things, to recording a gain on debt forgiveness for Agora Place Osaka Namba as extraordinary income.

entries.d7cb1f757db9c909: This is the central reportable segment of the company group, which operates hotels and ryokan. The securities report lists five facilities that the company operates and manages: 'Hotel Agora Osaka Moriguchi', 'Hotel Agora Regency Osaka Sakai' and 'Dorsett by Agora Osaka Sakai' in Osaka Prefecture, and 'Agora Place Tokyo Asakusa' and 'Agora Tokyo Ginza' in Tokyo; it lists 'Agora Kyoto Karasuma' and 'Agora Kyoto Shijo' in Kyoto Prefecture and 'TSUKI' in Tokyo as facilities it operates under contract. Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥8,962 million (up 22.1% from the previous year), and segment profit was ¥1,395 million (up 99.7% from the previous year). The securities report states that, against the backdrop of the weaker yen, the number of foreign visitors to Japan increased (42,683,600 for the full year 2025), and that this drove its performance. In particular, in the Osaka area, the number of guests at 'Hotel Agora Regency Osaka Sakai' and 'Hotel Agora Osaka Moriguchi' increased substantially due to higher demand for accommodation accompanying the Osaka-Kansai Expo. 'Dorsett by Agora Osaka Sakai' opened in March 2025, and 'Agora Place Osaka Namba' ended its operations at the end of July 2025.
